reasoning: Classify 1..100 by residue mod 7. Since 100 = 14*7 + 2, residues 1 and 2 each occur 15 times; residues 0,3,4,5,6 each occur 14 times. Two elements sum to a multiple of 7 iff their residues are complementary: (0,0), (1,6), (2,5), (3,4). So a valid subset contains at most one multiple of 7, and from each pair {1,6},{2,5},{3,4} it can use elements of only one residue class. Hence size <= 1 + 15 + 15 + 14 = 45. Construction: {7} ∪ {n ≡ 1 mod 7} ∪ {n ≡ 2 mod 7} ∪ {n ≡ 3 mod 7} = {7, 1,8,...,99, 2,9,...,100, 3,10,...,94}, with 1+15+15+14 = 45 elements; any two distinct elements have residue sum in {1,...,6} mod 7, never 0.
